app.name: WorkLogger
dock.label: Sources for the day or month
toolbar.collectHelp: Read git history and calendar meetings for the range, then build drafts. The arrow has more.
toolbar.modulesHelp: Choose which data sources WorkLogger uses
toolbar.logInTempoHelp: Each ticket's days and durations, ready to copy into Tempo
toolbar.exportHelp: Export to Tempo, Markdown for Claude, CSV or JSON
lock.title: WorkLogger is locked
lock.body: Unlock to use your API tokens.
timesheet.help: Click a day to see its entries. Drag a line from a card (or an entry from the day panel) onto a workday to log it there, or use Move to… on the entry.
timesheet.nothingYet: Nothing logged yet. Collect, rebuild drafts, or add an entry.
timesheet.dragHint: Drag onto a day in the calendar to move this entry
review.emptyBody: Pick a range and choose Collect to read your commits and meetings.
worklog.estimateHelp: Raw estimate before scaling the day to its target
worklog.lockedHelp: Locked: kept when drafts are rebuilt
token.saved: Saved. Type a new one to replace it.
worklog.unlockedHelp: Unlocked: replaced when drafts are rebuilt
ticket.tickHelp: Ticking a day marks its entries as in Tempo: they are locked and drafts rebuilds leave them alone.
ticket.noIssueBody: These entries can't go to Tempo until they have a ticket.
ticket.emptyBody: Collect the month first; its tickets show up here.
totals.emptyBody: Collect worklogs on the Review page first.
sessions.emptyTitle: No work sessions in this range
sessions.emptyBody: Choose Fetch range to read them from HRmaster. Without sessions the default workday from Settings is used.
meetings.googleHelp: Read-only. Signs in in your browser; WorkLogger never sees your password.
meetings.googleWebHelp: Uses your Google Chat sign-in. Collect reads it too, as long as the API isn't connected.
meetings.googleWebSignIn: Sign in to Google Chat first (Chats page); the calendar uses the same Google sign-in.
meetings.icsHelp: Outlook and most calendars can publish a secret ICS address. Paste it here to read its meetings.
meetings.rulesHelp: An issue key in the meeting title or description wins, then the first matching rule, then the default issue.
meetings.oauth: Google Calendar API with your own OAuth client
meetings.oauthHelp: Only needed when your company's Google Workspace blocks the built-in sign-in. Requires a “Desktop app” OAuth client in Google Cloud.
meetings.emptyBody: Connect a calendar, then choose Read meetings.
meetings.ticketHelp: Type a ticket and press Enter: a rule logs “{title}” to it from now on
meetings.suggestion: “{title}” comes back {n} times without a ticket.
chats.emptyBody: Choose Paste export… and paste the exported chat history.
chats.selectBody: Its messages show here, oldest first.
chats.stretchHelp: {from} – {to} · messages close together count as one stretch
chats.alwaysHelp: Log this conversation to {issue} on every day it has messages
chats.pasteBody: Paste the base64 text of the export (zlib-compressed JSON) or the JSON itself.
repos.skippedHelp: Never scanned. A name like “archive” matches any folder with that name; a path like ~/Work/old matches that folder. Repositories already listed inside them are removed.
repos.projectsHelp: Tempo logs time to issues, so a repository assigned only to a project uses that project's catch-all issue.
repos.order: Commit message key → branch key → repository issue → project catch-all issue
repos.emptyBody: Choose your workspace folder to find its git repositories.
repos.removeHelp: Remove from the list (the repository on disk is not touched)
periods.subtitle: Book stretches of days to a larger project
periods.emptyBody: Add one here: every workday inside it is topped up to a full day with its issue.
periods.help: On every workday inside a period, your commits, Jira work and meetings keep their own issues, and the period's issue fills only the time still missing from the day. Its comment goes to Tempo with that time. Leave days are never filled. Later periods win where they overlap. Rebuild drafts after changing periods.
periods.name: Project name
settings.skinHelp: Dress the window as another system. The window buttons and shortcuts stay this computer's.
settings.displayHelp: Auto follows the system's accessibility settings.
settings.hoursPerDay: Hours per day without imported sessions
settings.weekends: Fill rest days without imported sessions too
settings.dailyHelp: A day adds up to the time you worked according to the imported work sessions (HRmaster's worked hours), rounded up: with 15 minutes, 7h 22m becomes 7h 30m and 12h stays 12h. Days without imported sessions use the hours per day. Meetings keep their real length; commit entries fill the rest.
settings.absencesHelp: Leave days (Szabadság and other leave codes) are logged with the hours HRmaster reports; public holidays only when it reports hours. Rest days, holidays and leave never get filled with commit time.
settings.ignoredPaths: Paths left out of the size estimate
settings.estimatesHelp: An estimate mixes the free working time since your previous commit with the size of the change (lines, files) and its kind (refactor, fix, typo…).
settings.chatGap: New stretch after a pause of (minutes)
settings.chatsHelp: Messages closer together than the pause count as one stretch of chatting; each stretch is at least a minute. Conversations listed here (ticked “Always” on the Chats page) are logged to their ticket on every day they have messages.
settings.sitesHelp: Each site has its own Chrome or Edge profile inside WorkLogger, separate from your everyday browser; Sign out deletes its cookies. HRmaster ends its session after about 25 idle minutes, so it often shows signed out; a fetch then asks you to sign in.
jira.accountsHelp: Each issue goes to the account whose projects include its key (PROJ-12 → PROJ); keys no account has go to the default account, which also gives the exports their Jira link.
jira.name: Name
jira.footer: Used to show what is already logged and for Export → Send. With Another tool, WorkLogger only exports files and checklists for this account's issues. Log in Tempo by ticket works without any key. Tokens are stored in your system keyring.
module.git.summary: Commits from your git repositories, estimated from their size and timing.
module.calendar.summary: Meetings from Google Calendar or a calendar feed, with their real length.
module.workTimes.summary: Your worked hours from HRmaster, so every day adds up to HR's records.
module.chats.summary: Stretches of chatting in Google Chat, logged to the conversation's ticket.
module.jira.summary: Tickets you created, changed or commented on, sharing the day with your other work.
welcome.title: Welcome to WorkLogger
welcome.body: Choose where your working time comes from, and how it gets into Tempo. You can change this any time with Modules.
welcome.how: How do you log in Tempo?
welcome.byHand: By hand, one ticket at a time. No API key: WorkLogger lists each ticket's days to copy.
welcome.api: Send with the Tempo API. Needs a Tempo token and Jira email in Settings.
export.title: Export {from} – {to}
export.claudeHelp: A Markdown checklist with instructions: give it to Claude and it fills your Tempo timesheet in the browser.
export.pushByDay: Send the period's reviewed entries at once, or one day at a time under Days. Days that still have drafts are left out.
export.footer: After entering the worklogs in Tempo yourself (or via Claude), mark them exported so they aren't sent twice.
activity.title: Background activity
activity.empty: Nothing has run in the background yet.
nav.label: Sections
toolbar.label: Month
status.label: Status
review.selectHint: Click to select, Shift- or Ctrl-click for more; right-click for actions.
worklog.commentPlaceholder: What you did, as Tempo should show it
worklog.commentHelp: This text goes to Tempo. An entry needs it before it can be marked reviewed.
worklog.reviewNeedsComment: Write the comment for Tempo to mark this entry reviewed.
profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.help: The accounts WorkLogger reads from and logs to. Add as many of a kind as you need: every Google and HRmaster profile is read and merged.
profiles.help.googleChat: A Google account: its Chat messages, and its calendar when the Calendar API isn't connected. Several Google accounts can be signed in at once; the address picks this one.
profiles.help.hrmaster: An HRmaster site: your work sessions. With several, each day comes from the one that has it.
profiles.help.tempo: Tempo for one Jira profile's issues. The token is kept in your system keyring.
profiles.empty: No profiles yet. Add the accounts you work with.
profiles.tempoNeedsJira: Tempo logs for a Jira profile: add a Jira profile first (each one can have one Tempo profile).
calendars.apiHelp: Read-only, with your own sign-in in the browser.
calendars.signInProfile: Sign in to a Google profile (Settings → Profiles); its calendar is read with that sign-in.
calendars.addProfile: Add a Google profile in Settings → Profiles to read its calendar without API keys.
sessions.noProfile: Add an HRmaster profile in Settings → Profiles to read your work sessions.
repos.foldersHelp: Every folder is scanned for git repositories; the skipped folders below apply to all of them.
welcome.intro: WorkLogger fills your Tempo timesheet from what you actually did. Each month goes like the sidebar:
welcome.flow.setup: Tell WorkLogger where your work is: repository folders, calendars and the accounts you use.
welcome.flow.gather: Collect brings in the month: commits, meetings, HR work sessions and chats.
welcome.flow.fill: Every day is filled up to the hours you worked. Review the entries and give each a Jira ticket.
welcome.flow.finish: Copy each ticket's days into Tempo by hand, or send them all with the Tempo API.
welcome.setupBody: Do these one at a time; each button takes you to the right place. This list stays on Settings → Profiles until everything is set up.
setup.title: Getting started
setup.help: What your data sources still need. Each button takes you to the right place.
setup.nothing: Nothing to set up for the chosen sources. Choose Collect to bring in the month.
setup.repositories.help: On Repositories, add the folders that hold your git repositories and the email addresses you commit with.
setup.google.help: A Google profile with your address, then Sign in: Chats are read in its window.
setup.calendar.help: A Google profile's calendar, the Google Calendar API, or an .ics feed on Settings → Calendars.
setup.hrmaster.help: An HRmaster profile with your company's address, then Sign in: work sessions are read in its window.
setup.jira.help: A Jira profile: the site's address, your Atlassian email and an API token.
setup.tempo.help: A Tempo profile for the Jira profile, with a Tempo API token.
jira.tokenTitle: What the Jira API token needs
jira.tokenStep.create: Create it at id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens.
jira.tokenStep.email: Enter the email address of the same Atlassian account above.
jira.tokenStep.classic: A classic token (without scopes) works with your own Jira permissions.
jira.tokenStep.scoped: A token with scopes needs read:jira-user and read:jira-work, plus write:jira-work to send worklogs to Jira. WorkLogger reaches it through api.atlassian.com, as Atlassian requires.
tempo.tokenTitle: What the Tempo API token needs
tempo.tokenStep.create: Create it in Tempo → Settings → API Integration → New token.
tempo.tokenStep.view: View worklogs: to show what is already in Tempo.
tempo.tokenStep.manage: Manage worklogs: for Send to Tempo.
tempo.tokenStep.url: Tempo address: https://api.tempo.io/4, or your region's (e.g. https://api.eu.tempo.io/4).
filter.label: Filter
filter.noMatchBody: Try other words or another day.
repos.noCommitsBody: None of your repositories has commits on this day or in this month. Collect, or show them all to set them up.
overview.emptyBody: Collect reads git history, meetings and chats for the month, then builds draft entries.
overview.doneBody: Every workday is logged, has tickets and is in Tempo.
overview.todo.logInTempoDetail: Grouped by ticket, ready to send or copy

days.needComments.one: {n} draft needs a comment for Tempo before it can be reviewed.
days.needComments.other: {n} drafts need a comment for Tempo before they can be reviewed.

days.sendHelp: Sends this day's reviewed entries to Tempo. What Tempo already has for the day is left out.
days.sendNeedsReview: Review every draft of the day before sending it to Tempo.
days.sendDetail: They are created under your Jira account. Entries Tempo already has for the day are left out.
days.emptyBody: No entries for this day yet. Collect again, or add entries by hand.
days.freeBody: No work is expected on this day. Add an entry if you worked anyway.
days.happenedHelp: Meetings and chats collected for the day. Click a ticket to use it for the selected entry, or for the entries without one.
week.pick: Go to the week of a day
msg.busy: Another collect or fetch is still running.
msg.calendar.exportUnreadable: Google Calendar: the export could not be read.
msg.calendar.needGoogle: Add a Google profile in Settings → Profiles, or connect the Calendar API.
msg.calendar.notYours: Google Calendar ({name}): none of the calendars ({calendars}) is yours; enter the profile's Google address in Settings → Profiles.
msg.calendar.notZip: Google Calendar: the export is not a zip file.
msg.calendar.read: Read {n} meetings. Rebuild drafts to apply them.
msg.chat.fetchCancelled: Cancelled. Google Chat: {messages} new messages in {conversations} conversations.
msg.chat.fetched: Google Chat: {messages} new messages in {conversations} conversations.
msg.chat.future: Google Chat: these days haven't come yet.
msg.chat.notRecognized: Paste the base64 text of the chat export, or its JSON.
msg.chat.pageChanged: Google Chat's page changed; the message list could not be read.
msg.chat.searchFailed: Google Chat's search request failed ({reason}); Chat may have changed.
msg.chat.searchUnreadable: Google Chat: the search answer could not be read.
msg.chat.tooShort: This chat is too short to log.
msg.collect.needEmail: Add your commit email address under Repositories so only your commits are counted.
msg.collect.jira: Collected your work on {tickets} Jira ticket-days for {from} – {to}.
msg.collect.meetingsJira: Collected {meetings} meetings and your work on {tickets} Jira ticket-days for {from} – {to}.
msg.google.needProfile: Add a Google profile in Settings → Profiles first.
msg.jira.needProfile: Add a Jira profile with its API token in Settings → Profiles to read your Jira activity.
msg.google.notConfigured: Add the Google OAuth client ID and secret first.
msg.google.timedOut: Google sign-in timed out. Try connecting again.
msg.hrmaster.imported: HRmaster: imported {n} days. Rebuild drafts to apply them.
msg.hrmaster.needAddress: Enter the HRmaster address of {name} in Settings → Profiles first.
msg.hrmaster.needProfile: Add an HRmaster profile with your company's address in Settings → Profiles first.
msg.hrmaster.unreadable: HRmaster: the page could not be read.
msg.locked.google: Unlock first: the Google sign-in is kept in the keyring.
msg.locked.tokens: Unlock first: tokens are kept in the keyring.
msg.missing.ids: The issue or the Jira account id is missing.
msg.missing.jiraAccount: Add a Jira profile in Settings → Profiles first.
msg.missing.jiraSite: Enter the Jira site address in Settings → Profiles.
msg.missing.jiraToken: Enter the Jira email and API token in Settings → Profiles.
msg.missing.start: The worklog has no start time.
msg.missing.tempoToken: Enter the Tempo API token in Settings → Profiles.
msg.missing.tempoUrl: The Tempo API address isn't a valid URL. Check it in Settings → Profiles.
msg.missing.url: The Jira site address isn't a valid URL. Check it in Settings → Profiles.
msg.period.backwards: The period “{title}” ends before it starts.
msg.profile.tempoTaken: That Jira profile already has a Tempo profile.
msg.push.dayDone: Sent {n} worklogs for {day} to Tempo ({already} already there, left out).
msg.push.dayHasDrafts: {day} still has {n} draft entries. Review them before sending the day to Tempo.
msg.push.future: {day} hasn't come yet; only past days and today can be sent to Tempo.
msg.rule.needText: Enter the text to look for.
msg.site.reloading: {name}: the page kept reloading while it was read.
msg.site.signedOut: {name} is signed out. Sign in in its window, then fetch again.
msg.worklog.badDuration: “{text}” is not a duration. Try 1h 30m, 1.5h or 90.
msg.worklog.needComments: {n} of the entries have no comment for Tempo yet. Write them before marking them reviewed.
msg.worklog.needsComment: Write the comment that goes to Tempo before marking the entry reviewed.
msg.worklog.sent: This entry is already in Tempo; change it there.
plans.notReadBody: Choose Read Tempo. Plans come from Tempo Planner with your Jira profile's Tempo token; Jira or Tempo adds them when a ticket is assigned to you or changes status.
plans.emptyBody: Tempo has no planned time for you this month, and no worklogs that WorkLogger didn't send.
plans.plannedHelp: Time Tempo Planner has for this ticket on this day
plans.kindTempoHelp: A worklog Tempo already has that WorkLogger didn't send (logged by Jira, Tempo or by hand)
plans.nothingLogged: Nothing in WorkLogger on this ticket that day.

plans.untagged.one: {n} entry this day has no ticket
plans.untagged.other: {n} entries this day have no ticket

plans.useHelp: {key} is planned for you in Tempo this day
tasks.title: Tasks
days.fetchChat: Fetch Google Chat for this day
week.fetchChat: Fetch Google Chat for this week
jira.noAccountBody: Add a Jira profile with an API token in Settings → Profiles to see what you did in Jira.
jira.emptyBody: You didn't create, change or comment on any issue this month.

jira.suggest.one: {n} entry without a ticket ran around this — {key}?
jira.suggest.other: {n} entries without a ticket ran around this — {key}?

onboard.intro: Tell WorkLogger what you use, and set each one up here. You can change all of it later in Settings.
onboard.q.git: Do you commit to Git repositories?
onboard.q.git.help: Your commits become worklogs. Choose the folders that hold your repositories.
onboard.q.hrmaster.help: Your work sessions set how many hours each day needs.
onboard.q.googleChat.help: Your messages show what you worked on.
onboard.q.jira: Do you use Jira and Tempo?
onboard.q.jira.help: Read your Jira issues, and send worklogs to Tempo with its API.
onboard.q.jiraWork: Do you plan or analyse work in Jira (BA, PM)?
onboard.q.jiraWork.help: Tickets you write, refine, move or comment on become worklogs, next to your meetings.
onboard.page.hrmaster: Add your HRmaster site and sign in.
onboard.page.googleChat: Add your Google account and sign in.
onboard.page.jira: Add your Jira site, email and API token.
onboard.page.tempo: Add your Tempo token for this Jira profile.
onboard.needOne: Set up at least one of them to start: a repository folder or an account.

collect.settled.one: {n} day was left out: Tempo has its week in full. Press Collect again to fetch it anyway.
collect.settled.other: {n} days were left out: Tempo has their weeks in full. Press Collect again to fetch them anyway.

cleanup.hint.one: {n} day is in weeks Tempo has in full: its commits, meetings and chat messages can be removed from this computer. The worklogs stay.
cleanup.hint.other: {n} days are in weeks Tempo has in full: their commits, meetings and chat messages can be removed from this computer. The worklogs stay.

cleanup.done: Cleaned up {days} days in Tempo: {rows} commits, meetings and messages removed.
msg.collect.allSettled: Tempo already has {from} – {to} in full, so nothing was collected.
module.confluence.summary: Pages and blog posts you wrote, edited or commented on, with a suggested time from when you worked on them.
profiles.help.confluence: A Confluence site: the pages you work on. Link a Jira profile on the same site to use its email and token, or give it its own.
setup.confluence.help: A Confluence profile, linked to your Jira profile or with its own site, email and API token.
confluence.tokenStep.linked: Linked to a Jira profile, the Jira token is used, unless you enter one here.
confluence.tokenStep.classic: A classic API token (without scopes) works for both Jira and Confluence, with your own permissions.
confluence.tokenStep.scoped: A token with scopes is made for one app: a Jira one doesn't work here. Create one for Confluence with search:confluence, read:confluence-user and read:page:confluence (all read-only). WorkLogger reaches it through api.atlassian.com.
confluence.tokenStep.own: Create it at id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens. It is kept in your system keyring.
msg.collect.confluence: Collected your work on {pages} Confluence page-days for {from} – {to}.
msg.confluence.needProfile: Add a Confluence profile in Settings → Profiles to read your Confluence pages.

confluence.summary.one: {n} edit or comment on {p} pages this month
confluence.summary.other: {n} edits and comments on {p} pages this month

confluence.emptyBody: You didn't edit or comment on any page this month.
msg.missing.confluenceSite: Enter the Confluence site, or link a Jira profile, in Settings → Profiles.
confluence.noChanges: No versions of yours on this day any more.
module.email.summary: The mail you send, by subject: a few minutes each, booked to a ticket named in the subject.
profiles.help.email: A mailbox read over IMAP: only the subjects and times in its Sent folder, read-only. The password is kept in your system keyring.
setup.email.help: An Email profile: the IMAP server, your user name and a password (an app password for Gmail, iCloud or Yahoo).
email.passwordStep.read: WorkLogger opens only the Sent folder, read-only, and reads each mail's subject and time; never the text or the recipients.
email.passwordStep.app: Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an app password (with two-step sign-in on), not your account password. Gmail also needs IMAP switched on in its settings.
email.passwordStep.microsoft: Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com accept only Microsoft's own sign-in for IMAP, so a password doesn't work there.
email.passwordStep.server: The server is reached over TLS on port 993 unless you give another (imap.example.com:1993).
email.emptyBody: Nothing collected for this month. Collect reads the mail you sent.
email.failedTitle: Sent mail could not be shown
msg.collect.email: Collected your mail in {threads} thread-days for {from} – {to}.
msg.email.needProfile: Add an Email profile in Settings → Profiles to read the mail you sent.
msg.email.needServer: Enter the mail server and your user name in Settings → Profiles.
msg.email.needPassword: Enter the mail password (an app password for Gmail, iCloud or Yahoo) in Settings → Profiles.
commits.title: Commits
commits.failed: The commits could not be read.
commits.noneBody: This entry wasn't made from commits, or they are no longer stored (collect the day again).
commits.truncated: The changes are too long to show whole; the rest is cut off.
picker.title: Choose a ticket · {day}
picker.search: Filter, or search Jira with Enter
picker.noneKnown: No tickets used in this period or the months before it.
picker.noMatch: None of them matches. Search Jira below.
picker.jiraNone: Jira has no issue created in this window that matches.
picker.jiraHelp: Search Jira for issues created around the day, with the words above in their summary (or a key in full).
picker.stale: These are for an earlier search; search again for the current text or window.
worklog.chooseIssueHelp: Choose from the tickets of this period and before, or search Jira
msg.jira.searchNeedProfile: Add a Jira profile with its API token in Settings → Profiles to search Jira.
msg.commit.badHash: That is not a commit hash.
msg.commit.noRepo: The commit's repository is no longer in WorkLogger.
msg.commit.notFound: The commit could not be read from {repo}; it may have been rebased away or the repository moved.
week.send: Send the week's reviewed entries to Tempo

push.rangeQuestion.one: Send {n} reviewed worklog ({d}) for {from} – {to} to Tempo?
push.rangeQuestion.other: Send {n} reviewed worklogs ({d}) on {days} days for {from} – {to} to Tempo?

push.rangeDetail: They are created under your Jira account. Entries Tempo already has for those days are left out.

push.rangeDrafts.one: {n} day still has drafts and is left out: {days}.
push.rangeDrafts.other: {n} days still have drafts and are left out: {days}.

push.rangeLater.one: {n} entry on a day that hasn't come yet is left out.
push.rangeLater.other: {n} entries on days that haven't come yet are left out.

msg.push.rangeDone: Sent {n} worklogs for {from} – {to} to Tempo ({already} already there, left out; {drafts} days with drafts and {later} entries on later days not sent).
onboard.welcome.title: Your Tempo timesheet, filled from what you did
onboard.welcome.intro: Every month goes the same way:
onboard.welcome.collect.help: Commits, meetings, HR hours and chats come in.
onboard.welcome.check.help: Days fill up to your hours. Add a ticket where one is missing.
onboard.welcome.log.help: Copy each ticket's days by hand, or send them with the Tempo API.
onboard.welcome.time: Setup takes a few minutes. You can change everything later.
onboard.gitEmail: Leave the commit emails empty to use the one in your git config.
onboard.collect.title: Collecting {month}
onboard.collect.later: Left for later, on Sources → Finish setup
